messages:
alice: FYI we hit a nasty surprise bringing up a community Llama variant in the multi-model flow. standalone inference OK, but when we switch mid-session to a Mistral-compiled variant the outputs go noisy.
frank: noisy how? token misalignment or embedding mismatch?
alice: token misalignment. Reproducer: start session on model L (llama int4 quant), then hot-swap to model M (mistral-compiled). kvcache indices look aligned but attention replies are garbled.
charlie: could be head-order or head-packing differences. did you diff the per-head rotary phases and head strides?
alice: I compared the first few kv vectors. Example dump: 
```
# after switch
kvs[0][:6] = [0x0a1b, 0x0a1c, 0x0a1d, 0x0a1e, ...]
# expected (from original session)
kvs_expected[0][:6] = [0x0a1b, 0x0a1c, 0x0a1d, 0x0a1e, ...]
# rotary phases
rotary_L = [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, ...]
rotary_M = [0.0, 0.2501, 0.5002, 0.7501, ...]
```
frank: tiny numeric diffs shouldn't cause total failure unless the mapping across heads is wrong.
diane: check kernel export metadata - some int4 exports pack heads in groups which changes memory layout. If routing assumes contiguous head dims, indices will be off by stride.
charlie: don't forget tokenizer normalization differences. I saw Qwen builds apply NFKC normalization while others are identity. that changes token ids for certain diacritics / soft-hyphen and causes cache aliasing.
alice: ran a tokenizer audit (python -m tokencheck). Qwen variants normalized to NFKC, Gemma/Llama kept raw. Small differences cause re-tokenization mid-session.
frank: so two independent failure modes: tokenizer normalization -> different token ids, and head-layout/rotary -> kv index mismatch. Both can yield bad completions if we reuse the same cache.
diane: also watch quant packing. In recent int4 exports we observed grouped-head packing (pack factor 4) and an export flag `head_layout=packed`. If not annotated, runtime will misinterpret strides.
alice: quick mitigation: invalidate kvcache on any model-variant switch that differs in tokenizer normalization or head_layout. cheap and buys time.
infra-bot: rollout: added default route behavior to invalidate kvcache-on-variant-change for eng-ml-canary at 09:12 UTC :white_check_mark:
alice: after adding invalidation, evals look much better. before invalidation 50-shot summarization BLEU ~9.3, after invalidation ~27.9 (baseline ~28.1). nll and ppl drops concentrated on long-context (>1024) tests.
eval-bot: eval snapshot: baseline BLEU 28.1, post-invalidate BLEU 27.9, no-invalidate BLEU 9.3. regression correlates with sessions that attempted cache reuse across incompatible variants.
frank: good evidence it's cache aliasing, not model quality.
diane: long-term fix: we should include canonical fields in model export metadata: token_norm: NFKC|NFC|NONE, head_layout: contiguous|packed, rotary_scheme: per_head|per_pair, pack_factor: int. routing should block cache reuse unless these match within tolerance.
charlie: additionally add a small shim to the routing layer that runs a fast tokenization check on the first 32 tokens when switching: if token ids diverge, force re-tokenize and invalidate.
alice: I'll open a PR with three changes: 1) default invalidate-on-variant-switch, 2) model-export metadata enforcement in router, 3) token-normalizer shim for legacy models to emulate canonical form.
frank: add unit tests: create sessions that rely on soft-hyphen/token-normalization differences and assert we invalidate. also test switching between contiguous vs packed head layouts to ensure we reject reuse.
diane: I'll inventory onboarded models and flag those with nonstandard token_norm or packed head_layout. volunteering to coordinate with teams.
alice: running scanner now; initial targets gemma-lite, qwen-2x, mistralx-nightly. will post a table later.
charlie: once we consider re-enabling cache reuse across variants, add a fuzz-check that compares kv keys and rotary phases within an epsilon and log discrepancies before allowing reuse. silent drift is dangerous.
alice: agreed. will include epsilon gating and verbose logging for the first release. tagging @diane for rollout timeline.
